recipes.name: Eggs in a Nest inspired by Lots of Stuff
instructions: In a bowl, combine warm (110°F) water with one packet of instant yeast and the all purpose flour along with sugar, salt, and unsalted butter at room temperature. - 100 ml water - packet of instant yeast - 325 g all purpose flour divided - 50 g sugar - 5 g salt - 45 g unsalted butter divided

Stir to combine before adding water and stirring to create a pancake batter like paste, and then add the remaining flour and stir until a shaggy dough forms. - 300 ml water - 325 g all purpose flour divided
Turn out onto a counter top and knead for 7-9 minutes until a smooth supple dough forms.
Generously oil a large bowl and place the dough inside. Roll the dough around a little to make sure it’s evenly coated in oil. - A little oil
Cover with plastic wrap and let sit at room temperature for 45 minutes to an hour until the dough has doubled in size. - Plastic wrap

Turn out onto a lightly floured countertop and punch down until it’s back to its original size and then start forming into a loaf. Make sure to tuck it under itself to make sure it gets that nice loaf top.
Place in a loaf pan that is coated with butter and parchment paper and loosely cover with plastic wrap. Let sit at room temperature for one hour until it has doubled in size. - Parchment paper
Brush the loaf down with butter and place in a 400° oven for 25-35 minutes.
Remove from the oven and brush it down again with some more butter and let sit overnight.
For the Egg In The Nest
Cut some thick slices of bread and use a glass to stamp out the center of the bread. Keep the center piece of bread for mopping up afterward. - Bread

Heat a pan and melt butter. Place bread in the pan and make sure both sides are evenly coated before plopping down and letting it sit for about 2 minutes on medium low heat. - 45 g unsalted butter divided
Place a dollop of bacon fat inside the circle before cracking one egg into the center. Crank the heat up to medium high, and let sit for 1 minute before flipping the bread and egg. - Bacon fat - Eggs
Cook for 10-15 seconds on other side while coating with salt and pepper for taste. Also be sure to place your bread center in the pan to quickly crisp it up on either side. - Pepper - Salt
Put on a plate and enjoy!
